summary: One more source-decided finding is worth recording while the budget lasts, and it sits on the same handler as the last three: every request that arrives on the consumer channel goes through processRPC, which runs checkRPCHeader first and answers with an error instead of dispatching when the command has no header or when its protocol version is outside the accepted range or more than one version behind the node, but the heartbeat fast path calls appendEntries straight from processHeartbeat and never runs that gate. The network transport's classification is a shape test - a term, a leader address, a zero previous entry and term, no entries, a zero leader commit index - and imposes no version requirement, so a peer advertising an unsupported protocol version can still have its heartbeat processed. Processing it is not inert: appendEntries adopts the higher term, sets the node to follower and records the sender as leader, which is exactly the effect the gate denies every other path. I recorded the behaviour with both paths cited, wrote the interpretation as explained with the scope stated honestly - the fast path still cannot append entries or advance the commit index, and a supported peer at a higher term would have produced the same transition, so this is not new authority but a node acting on a message it would drop as unsupported elsewhere, which is what the compatibility check exists to prevent - and kept four counterweights, including that this is a code-structure claim with no execution behind it and that the harnesses in this run reach the handler through a wrapper transport rather than the socket path where the classification lives. The rest of the run's record is unchanged: six witnessed behaviours including the durable term regression with its reproduction and causal control, the conditional account of when that regression can arise and the registered question about asymmetric write latencies, two uninstrumented probes bounding its natural rate at zero falls in 792 and 768 deliveries, the scoped log-cache negative, and the two knowledge corrections.
